description: We are Team NABULA, a group of university students passionate about environmental science, satellite technology, and innovation. Our project focuses on harmonizing NASA MODIS and VIIRS fire observations to analyze historical fire activity through an interactive web application. We welcome participants interested in Earth science, data analysis, programming, GIS, and data visualization to collaborate and contribute to our project.
summary:
NABULA — From Space to Fire Intelligence

NABULA is an interactive web application developed to analyze historical fire activity using NASA's MODIS and VIIRS satellite observations. It addresses the challenge of comparing data from sensors with different spatial resolutions and detection capabilities by organizing observations within a common spatial and temporal framework.

Using historical data from NASA FIRMS, NABULA provides an interactive Fire Explorer map, SensorBridge for comparing MODIS and VIIRS observations, and FireTime, a Burning Activity Calendar that visualizes daily and seasonal fire patterns. The application also includes Fire Insights, which helps users explore historical trends and identify unusual activity.

By presenting satellite observations through interactive maps, standardized geographical grids, calendars, and analytical visualizations, NABULA makes complex environmental data more accessible and easier to interpret.

The project aims to support environmental research, improve understanding of historical fire activity, and contribute to better environmental planning and fire preparedness, initially focusing on Saudi Arabia with the potential for global expansion.
details:
NABULA — Project Details

NABULA (From Space to Fire Intelligence) is an interactive web application developed for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 to address the challenge of harmonizing MODIS and VIIRS satellite fire observations.

How It Works

NABULA uses historical active-fire observations from NASA FIRMS. These records include geographical coordinates, detection dates, and satellite measurements.

The application organizes MODIS and VIIRS observations within a common spatial and temporal framework, allowing users to compare historical fire activity despite differences in sensor resolution and detection capabilities.

The application includes four main features:

  • Fire Explorer: An interactive geographical map that displays satellite-detected fire hotspots and allows users to explore different regions and time periods.
  • SensorBridge: A satellite comparison tool that presents MODIS and VIIRS observations using standardized spatial and temporal units, supporting more consistent historical analysis.
  • FireTime: An interactive Burning Activity Calendar that visualizes daily fire activity and allows users to compare seasonal and yearly patterns.
  • Fire Insights: A data analysis section that presents historical trends and helps users investigate unusual changes in fire activity.

Technologies Used

NABULA was developed using Next.js, React, and TypeScript for the interactive web application, with Vercel for deployment. NASA FIRMS provides the satellite fire observation datasets, while interactive mapping and geographical data processing support the visualization and comparison of fire activity.

Innovation and Creativity

What makes NABULA distinctive is its focus on comparing fire observations from two satellite sensors with different spatial resolutions: MODIS (approximately 1 km) and VIIRS (375 m).

Rather than simply displaying raw hotspot locations, NABULA organizes observations using a common geographical grid, including 10 km grid-cell analysis, and presents the results through synchronized maps, calendars, and analytical visualizations.

This approach helps users understand sensor-related differences and explore historical fire activity patterns more clearly.

Benefits and Intended Impact

NABULA aims to support environmental researchers, land managers, environmental authorities, and emergency preparedness professionals by making historical satellite fire information easier to access and interpret.

The application can help users investigate seasonal burning patterns, explore areas with recurring fire detections, and support environmental research and planning.

The initial demonstration focuses on Saudi Arabia, with the potential to expand to other regions worldwide.

Challenges and Considerations

During development, we considered differences in satellite detection sensitivity, spatial resolution, historical data coverage, and the challenges of interpreting fire hotspot observations.

We also considered the importance of distinguishing satellite detections from individual fire events and ensuring that the information presented is scientifically meaningful.

NABULA currently focuses on historical fire analysis rather than predicting future fires. Future improvements may include near-real-time data integration, automated anomaly notifications, and additional environmental analysis tools.
